text:
Sam: hey! first day. using Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu) and VS Code Remote. installed asdf in WSL but my npm installs are hitting our corporate Nexus and failing auth. also sometimes node commands run from Windows path instead of WSL. any standard checklist? :wave:
DevX Bot: welcome Sam! paste `which node` (in WSL), `echo $PATH`, and `cat ~/.npmrc` (if present). Also say if you launched VS Code from Windows or from WSL.
Sam: which node -> /usr/bin/node, echo $PATH -> /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/games:/usr/local/bin:/home/sam/.asdf/shims, launched VS Code via remote-WSL icon (so server in WSL). ~/.npmrc has `registry=https://nexus.corp.redwood/registry/` and `//nexus.corp.redwood/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}`
Anika: sounds like two things: (1) asdf not picking the installed node version (shim pointing to system), (2) NPM_TOKEN not set in environment inside WSL/VS Code. For (1) check `asdf current` and `.tool-versions`. For (2 we keep tokens in 1password and the dotfiles use direnv to expose NPM_TOKEN to the shell).
Rahul: run `asdf plugin-list && asdf list nodejs` to see installed versions. If none, run `asdf plugin-add nodejs` then `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0 && asdf global nodejs 18.16.0 && asdf reshim`. If `which node` still shows /usr/bin/node, ensure ~/.asdf/shims is before /usr/bin in PATH (in WSL edit ~/.profile or ~/.bashrc depending on login shell).
Sam: did `asdf install` and set global. `which node` now -> /home/sam/.asdf/shims/node but `npm publish` still errors with 401 from Nexus. npm -v -> 9.6.1.
Anika: error 401 usually means NPM_TOKEN not present or not valid. Our dotfiles put a `.envrc` that reads secrets from 1password: `export NPM_TOKEN=$(op item get "npm-token" --fields label=token --raw)`. Did you run `op signin` in WSL and `direnv allow`?
Sam: I signed into 1password on Windows app but haven't used op in WSL. tried `op signin` in WSL and it prompted for account; after signin `echo $OP_SESSION_redwood` prints a token. ran `direnv allow` and now `echo $NPM_TOKEN` shows token. tried `npm whoami --registry=https://nexus.corp.redwood/registry/` and it returns my username. `npm publish` still fails with 403 CSRF-ish message.
Rahul: check your ~/.npmrc entries: avoid both `_authToken` and username/password combos. It should be `//nexus.corp.redwood/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}` and no auth lines elsewhere. Also ensure no Windows ~/.npmrc (like C:\Users\Sam\.npmrc) leaking into WSL env; VS Code sometimes mounts HOME differently. Run `npm config list --json` to see effective config.
Sam: ran `npm config list --json` in WSL; shows registry and authToken set from env. looked up the registry docs: Nexus sometimes requires `always-auth=true` or a token scoped to registry. trying with `npm publish --registry=https://nexus.corp.redwood/registry/ --_authToken=$NPM_TOKEN` still 403.
IT Helpdesk: if your token was recently rotated there is a propagation delay. Also check your account permissions on Nexus. I can verify your token if you ping me in a DM (don't paste tokens here).
Anika: another cross-check: do `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $NPM_TOKEN" https://nexus.corp.redwood/service/rest/v1/status` (or the registry health endpoint) to confirm token works at HTTP level. If curl gets 200, it's npm client config quirk.
Sam: curl returns 200 with that header. so token is good. npm publish still 403 though.
Rahul: I've seen this when the package name scope doesn't match allowed scopes in Nexus. If your package is @redwood/somepkg and Nexus repo is not configured for scoped uploads, it blocks. Check package.json `name` field and confirm repo permissions. Also confirm package version hasn't been published already (conflict can show as 403).
Sam: package is @samlab/cli-helper, new version. IT Helpdesk said permissions looked OK. I changed package name to unscoped for a quick test and publish worked. so looks like Nexus config for scopes is the culprit. IT Helpdesk is going to open a ticket.
Anika: quick wins for future hires: (1) Use asdf inside WSL (not Windows node) if you're working in Remote-WSL. (2) Sign into 1password with CLI inside WSL and `direnv allow` before running npm/publish. (3) Dotfiles repo contains a sample ~/.npmrc and a check script `scripts/check-registry.sh` that validates token+scope.
Sam: great, thanks. last small Q: git over https fails with SSL verification inside corporate proxy sometimes. any standard setting?
IT Helpdesk: corporate MITM proxy injects their CA. Add the corp CA to WSL trust store: put the PEM into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp.crt and run `sudo update-ca-certificates`. For Git specifically you can set `git config --global http.sslCAInfo /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` after updating. If you're behind authenticated proxy, set `git config --global http.proxy http://proxy.corp:3128` (ask IT for creds or use system auth).
Sam: added CA and updated certs, git clone works. dotfiles cloned and ran `./setup.sh`. everything feels much better. thanks everyone! :tada:
DevX Bot: welcome again Sam! If you want a quick 1:1 walk through, @Anika and @Rahul have onboarding slots.
Anika: happy to pair on Nexus scope fix once IT gets the ticket. tag me.
IT Helpdesk: ticket opened: #INC-7891 for Nexus scope config. We'll update you there.
Sam: thanks all — excited to start. pinging @Anika for pairing later.
